newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine legislature deadlocked over '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Philippine legislature deadlocked over '97 budget.

text.p: The Philippine Senate and Lower House said on Thursday they could not agree on cuts proposed by the Senate in the 1997 national budget and had suspended discussions until next year.

A special session of the bicameral committee reconciling differences between the two bodies could be held in early January, according to a House of Representatives statement quoting Senate speaker Jose de Venecia and Rolando Andaya, chairman of the House Appropriations committee.
Congressmen said there would be no paralysis of government work due to the deadlock over the 1997 budget.

"Unlike the United States, the Philippines has automatic appropriations in the budget. So government employees can continue to receive salaries and this will not result in any paralysis," said Andaya.
Earlier this week, the Senate had decided to slash the 1997 budget by about 82.6 billion pesos to 392.35 billion pesos, most of which removed debt service payments.

"By not including the debt service fund in the new appropriations, we are avoiding the temptation of the legislators to use some of the amount to fund congressional initiatives as had been done in the past," Senator Ernesto Herrera, the Senate Finance Committee chairman, earlier said.

Congressmen said they would immediately file two special appropriation bills in January to cover the increase in government employees' salaries and the internal revenue allotment of local government units.
